findings.summary: EVERY PREDECESSOR CHAIN IN ALL 18 FIXTURES CARRIES EXACTLY ONE DELTA, so the fold's AGGREGATION over a predecessor is never exercised -- only its single term. MEASURED, one mutation applied alone to the staged bytes: Invariants.java:254 `inherited.merge(run.key(), run.lastOffset() + 1, Math::max)` -> `Math::min` leaves ALL 18 tests of this commit green (18/18 ran, BUILD SUCCESSFUL, `--rerun-tasks --no-build-cache` with `sequencer/build/test-results/test` deleted first). Run against the FULL 181-test sequencer tree the only thing that notices is `CommitProtocolSimulationTest#aCleanRunViolatesNothing`, which is an UNTRACKED M4.20 file -- verbatim the situation this commit's own transitive-hop test condemns at InvariantsAcrossChainsTest.java:335-337 (`The only thing in the tree that noticed was an UNTRACKED M4.20 file, which is no coverage at all`), one arm over. So the arm that decides HOW MUCH of a predecessor's history is inherited is pinned only for a one-commit predecessor, and a leader that commits twice before failing over is the normal case, not an edge. I also confirmed this is a genuine FALSE NEGATIVE and not merely an untested line, with a throwaway probe since deleted: epoch 1 = CONTINUE, delta(1,3,0) (0..2), delta(2,3,3) (3..5), Seal(3,2); epoch 2 = CONTINUE(0,1,3), delta(1,2,4) -- a successor REASSIGNING offsets 4 and 5. The staged checker reports I2. Under `Math::min` the inherited mark is 3 instead of 6, so 4 > 3 and the reassignment is reported as a `gap` -- I2 vanishes. That is the checker agreeing with a broken production, which is the single property the class exists for and the species of all four majors already recorded against this task.
findings.failure_scenario: A future edit to `inheritedOffsets` that folds the predecessor's deltas in the wrong direction -- `Math::min`, or keeping the FIRST delta's high-water mark instead of the last, which is the same shape as the first-seal/last-seal confusion this very commit fixes twice -- lands green through all 18 tests. M4.13's 1,000-seed sweep then runs with a checker that, for every takeover whose predecessor committed more than once, sees a cross-boundary REASSIGNMENT as a `gap`: the sweep reports zero I2 violations while offsets are handed to two different records, and NFR-11 plus acceptance criterion 4 are broken with the compensating control silent. That is the round-1 finding of this task recurring one method deeper. ⚠️ THE REMEDY IS TWO LINES AND I MEASURED IT, so a major here does NOT mean rule 12's split: in `aTakeoversTWOChainsAreCheckedACROSSTheirJoin` add `first.commit(new CommitRequest("pod1", 2, "seg/a2", counts(2)));` before `first.close()` and move the resume assertion from `isEqualTo(6)` to `isEqualTo(8)`. Measured: the staged checker stays green with that change (18/18, no failures) and `Math::min` then FAILS it with `Expecting empty but was: [Violation[invariant=gap, ... resumes at 8, skipping 2]]`. It also strengthens the positive control in the direction the class javadoc already claims, because the predecessor is driven through the production path rather than hand-built.

findings.summary: THE WITHIN-CHAIN HIGH-WATER MARK IS NEVER TESTED FOR MONOTONICITY, because no fixture in either class puts a THIRD delta after a rewind. MEASURED: `nextOffset.put(run.key(), Math.max(from, run.firstOffset() + run.recordCount()))` -> `nextOffset.put(run.key(), run.firstOffset() + run.recordCount())` (the defensive `Math.max` dropped) survives ALL 181 tests in the sequencer module -- not just this commit's 18, and not even the untracked M4.20 simulation notices. Confirmed as a real behaviour change with a throwaway probe since deleted: CONTINUE, delta(1,6,0) (0..5), delta(2,1,0) (rewind to 0), delta(3,2,4) (4..5 again). The staged checker reports TWO I2 violations; without the `Math.max` the running mark regresses to 1 after the rewind and the second reassignment is reported as a `gap` instead, so the count and the KIND are both wrong. Scoped minor rather than major because the FIRST rewind is still reported, so a defective chain never reads as clean -- what is lost is the count and the classification of everything after it.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.13 pins exact violation counts per seed (its row and M4.24's both say so). With this unconstrained, a checker whose running mark can regress reports a different NUMBER and a different KIND for any chain containing two or more reassignments -- the shape two concurrent writers on one chain actually produce -- so a regression fixture pinned to `hasSize(2)` or to `containsExactly("I2", "I2")` would be pinned to arithmetic nothing verifies. Closing it is one fixture of the shape above in `InvariantsTest`, asserting two I2 violations rather than one, which is the within-a-chain side of the seam and so belongs in that class.

findings.summary: THE SHARED FIXTURE IS IMPORTED AND THEN NOT USED, and the positive control re-inlines it. `import static binjava.sequencer.InvariantFixtures.start;` at line 4 is dead -- `grep -n start` finds only that import and `LocalSequencer.start(...)` at line 39, a different method -- while lines 35-39 rebuild byte-for-byte what `InvariantFixtures.start` does (same LeaseConfig, same 10s/3s, same FIXED_CLOCK, same `LocalSequencer.start(store, PREFIX, leases, 8)`, same pod name `pod1`). That is exactly the drift `InvariantFixtures`' own javadoc says the extraction exists to prevent -- `a delta that drifted in one would make the two halves disagree about what a chain even looks like, with both suites green` -- with the sequencer-construction half of it not actually shared. MEASURED, and the fixture is weakly constrained on its own: `LocalSequencer.start(store, PREFIX, leases, 8)` -> `..., 1)` inside `InvariantFixtures.start` leaves all 18 green, so `start` is pinned by exactly one test (`aTakeoversTWOChainsAreCheckedACROSSTheirJoin`, which does die if the lease TTL moves 10s -> 1s) and by nothing at all in `InvariantsTest`. For contrast the other three helpers ARE constrained by construction and I measured each: swapping `delta`'s `records`/`firstOffset` arguments kills 16 of 18; `counts(n)` -> a constant 1 kills the takeover test; `put`'s key argument is constrained only up to lexical order (a uniform `keyFor(seq + 100)` shift survives, correctly, since the checker decodes the sequence from the bytes and that is what the I1 fixture depends on).
findings.failure_scenario: Someone changes `InvariantFixtures.start` -- the lease durations, the trailing `8`, or the pod identity -- to serve a new across-the-join fixture, and `InvariantsTest`'s positive control silently keeps the old construction. The two classes then disagree about what `a chain a REAL sequencer produced` means while both stay green, which is the drift the shared file was created to make impossible, and the positive control is the one test in the suite whose entire job is to be the production baseline. One line closes it: call `start(store, "pod1")` at line 39 and delete the now-live import's dead status, or drop the import if the inlining is deliberate -- but the inlining is what makes the sharing claim untrue.

findings.summary: THE MOVE OFF THE WALL CLOCK IS UNFALSIFIABLE, and the backlog row lists it as a delivered fix. MEASURED: replacing `FIXED_CLOCK` with `java.time.Clock.systemUTC()` leaves all 18 tests green. Correctness-wise the fixture is RIGHT and the row's reasoning is right -- nothing here depends on expiry, so a wall clock only decided which failover branch ran -- and no assertion can see the difference, which is precisely why an agent instruction or a comment is the weakest available enforcement (gate-design rung 6/7 for something statable as a predicate over files). Noted rather than raised higher because it is a hygiene property, not behaviour, and because saying `two fixtures moved onto a stopped clock` in the row while nothing can detect the move back is the same shape as the `crossEpochOffsetsChecked()` claim this commit deletes for being unable to go false.
findings.failure_scenario: A later fixture in this package -- M4.20's simulation lives here and owns `SimulatedClock` -- reintroduces `Clock.systemUTC()` in a helper, and the suite stays green while a test's branch coverage becomes a function of whether the machine stalled past a 10s TTL. That is a flake whose failure mode is passing for the wrong reason, which no assertion in this file can catch. A rung-3 predicate would: one grep gate refusing `Clock.systemUTC()` under `sequencer/src/test/java/` now that a stopped clock and a `SimulatedClock` both exist there. It belongs on a gate row rather than in this commit.

answer_to_author: Changes requested on one major, and the major is a two-line fixture addition rather than a split -- I say that explicitly because rule 12 reads differently at this round count. All fifteen mutations the task's history names are DEAD, each measured alone against the staged bytes with test-results deleted and `--rerun-tasks --no-build-cache`, and each killed by the test its seam predicts: discarding the recursion's result at Invariants.java:247 -> offsetsAreInheritedTRANSITIVELYAcrossMORETHANONEHop (and the depth cap driven to 0 dies there too); the first-seal `break` reverted in the FOLD and reverted in checkLink -- SEPARATELY, as the row claims -- each dying in BOTH aSECONDSealPastAFencedWritersDeltaDoesNOTMoveTheBarrier and theFOLDStopsAtTheFIRSTSealEvenWhenTheLINKIsWellFormed, and I confirmed the two arms are distinguished rather than only their conjunction: last-seal-wins in checkLink makes the fork/second-seal fixture's LINK assertion pass while its `resumes at 8` detail assertion is what fails; deleting the `gap` else-if -> aDeltaResumingABOVETheHighWaterMark plus the second-seal fixture; `< from` -> `< from - 1` -> anOverlapOfEXACTLYONERecord and nothing else, so the one-record boundary is doing exactly the work the row claims; the I1, I5 and `chain` arms -> one test each; the `continuedAt`, `prevSeq` and NOT-SEALED arms -> one test each; the no-CONTINUE arm -> aChainCarryingDELTASWithNoCONTINUEAtAll; `firstAncestorWithDeltas` -> `return 0` -> aLATERChainDISOWNINGAPredecessor, so round 2's blocking finding is genuinely closed by a test rather than by a comment; gutting `neverOpened` -> offsetsAreINHERITEDAcrossAChainThatWasNeverOPENED (and `return true` takes five tests down); `lastOffset() + 1` -> `lastOffset()` -> four tests. ALL 18 TESTS ARE NON-VACUOUS -- every one kills at least one mutation, and I had to go looking for the two that the fifteen did not cover: aChainAREALSequencerProducedHasNoViolations and anOffsetThatOVERLAPSOneAlreadyAssigned both die on the false-positive direction (`< from` -> `<= from`, and the gap arm's `>` -> `>=`), which is the right job for a positive control and for a `containsExactly`. THE SEAM IS HONEST: every mutant died in the file its side of the seam predicts, with no cross-file surprises, and the one borderline fixture -- aChainCarryingDELTASWithNoCONTINUEAtAll builds a single chain, so it looks within-a-chain -- is on the correct side, because the predicate under test is `inheritedOffsets`' link arm and the property is the ABSENCE of a join. ON THE `assigned up to 6` ASSERTION: it earns its place, and I measured why rather than arguing it. Within that test it is the ONLY assertion that kills `lastOffset() + 1` -> `lastOffset()`: the mutant still reports I2 (2 < 5), so `contains("I2")` alone survives, and only the detail assertion notices that the mark named is 5 rather than epoch 1's real 6. It is not over-specification, it is the difference between `some I2` and `I2 against the high-water mark two hops back`, which is the whole claim of the test -- and the detail string is the checker's reporting surface, the thing a failing seed is identified by, so coupling to it is coupling to output rather than to structure. ON InvariantFixtures having no test of its own: correct, and it does not need one -- `delta` is pinned by 16 of 18, `counts` by the takeover assertion, `put` by everything (and only up to lexical key order, which is right, since the checker decodes the sequence from the bytes and the I1 fixture DEPENDS on key and content being allowed to disagree). The exception is `start`, which is TR-C: pinned by one test and re-inlined rather than called in the other class. NOTHING RESTS ON A SLEEP, SOCKET, FIXED PORT OR SYSTEM TEMP; the tier is T1 over MemoryBinStore and that is the right tier rather than a layering smell, because reading raw objects instead of asking a live CommitLog is the class's entire reason to exist; the `@Timeout(60, SEPARATE_THREAD)` on both classes is a guard, not an assertion. TWO PREVIOUSLY-DISCLOSED SURVIVORS RE-CONFIRMED, neither raised as a finding: `neverOpened`'s slot-0 precision (`sealed.sequence() == 0` dropped) survives all 18, which is what M4.23's row already says and owns; and `e.sequence() > upTo` -> `>= upTo` in the fold survives but is an EQUIVALENT mutant, since `upTo` is always a Seal's own sequence and no fixture has a delta sharing it. The two open findings the packet lists as R3-1 and R4-1 are closed by measurement, not by reading names: R4-1's transitive hop dies in offsetsAreInheritedTRANSITIVELY..., and both first-seal arms of R2-2 die separately. TR-B/TR-C/TR-D are minors and rule 11 says leave them; the same fixture gap that produced TR-A also produced TR-B -- no fixture anywhere in this commit has more than two deltas in one chain, or more than one in a predecessor -- so if you would rather close both at once, that is one fixture per class and still not a split.
